# ScreenExtend — full site content

> ScreenExtend is a free, cross-platform desktop app that turns any device with a browser — a phone, tablet, or spare laptop — into a wireless second monitor for a Windows PC or Mac. The screen is streamed directly between machines over WebRTC, with no client app to install on the second device.

Website: https://screenextend.app/
Operator: Sarvesh Madullapalli (United States)
Support: support@screenextend.app

---

## Hero

**Turn any screen into your screen.**

ScreenExtend makes a phone, tablet, or spare laptop act as an extended monitor, streamed straight from your PC over your Wi-Fi network.

Highlights: no client install · WebRTC streaming · works offline.

---

## How it works

1. **Open ScreenExtend.** It shows a QR code and a 6-digit session code for every network you're on.
2. **Scan the code.** Point a phone, tablet, or spare laptop at the code. It opens in the browser without anything to install.
3. **Enter the session code.** Type the 6 digits to pair. The host spins up a virtual display sized to your device.
4. **Drag across, like a cable.** The screen streams over WebRTC. Slide a window off the edge and it lands on your phone, just like a true second monitor.

---

## Under the hood (architecture)

- **GPU-encoded** — Capture is encoded on the host GPU with NVENC (Nvidia), Quick Sync (Intel), or VideoToolbox (Mac) and sent over WebRTC for low latency.
- **No client app** — The client is just a web page. Any device with a modern browser can become an extended monitor.
- **Encrypted** — Signaling and streaming run over HTTPS/WebRTC with a certificate generated at runtime.
- **Offline mode** — The host can start its own ad-hoc network, so devices connect with no router in reach.
- **Per-device** — Resolution scale, orientation, refresh rate, and quality are set independently for each screen.
- **Auto-discovery** — The host watches every network adapter and rebuilds join URLs and QR codes as things change.

---

## Inside the host app

- **Dashboard — Add a new device.** Every network you're on gets its own QR code and URL, plus an Anywhere tile for joining across networks. Scan, enter the code, and a fullscreen extended monitor appears.
- **Per-device control — Adjust each display.** Each connected device has live settings: resolution scale, orientation, refresh rate, and video quality. Adjust one without affecting the others, or remove it with ease.
- **Settings — Session settings.** Regenerate the one-time session code, start an offline hosted network with no router, set a disconnect timeout, and view debug logs.

---

## Download

Supports Windows, Mac, and Linux (Linux coming soon).

- **Windows** — minimum Windows Client 20H1 (May 2020) or Windows Server 20H2 (October 2020).
  - 64-bit EXE: https://github.com/ScreenExtend/ScreenExtend/releases/latest/download/ScreenExtend_x64-setup.exe
  - ARM EXE: coming soon.
- **Mac** — minimum macOS Catalina 10.15+ (October 2019).
  - Intel DMG: https://github.com/ScreenExtend/ScreenExtend/releases/latest/download/ScreenExtend_x64.dmg
  - Apple Silicon DMG: https://github.com/ScreenExtend/ScreenExtend/releases/latest/download/ScreenExtend_aarch64.dmg
- **Linux** (coming soon) — minimum Ubuntu 20.04 (April 2020). DEB / RPM / AppImage.

Running on an unsupported operating system? Email support@screenextend.app with your device information for a custom build.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**How do I use ScreenExtend?**
Run it on your PC, scan a QR code (or open the URL) on any other device, and enter the 6-digit session code. That device becomes an extended monitor.

**Is my data secure?**
Yes. Every session needs a one-time code to join, which you can regenerate anytime to lock out unknown devices, and the stream is encrypted.

**What resolution and refresh rate can it do? Can it game?**
Each device goes up to 200% scale and 500 Hz. Gaming works if your network keeps up; heavy high-refresh video needs a strong connection. HDR is coming in a future release.

**How many devices can connect at once?**
As many as you like; each one gets its own virtual display. Performance drops as you add more.

**How does offline mode work?**
In Settings, start the hosted network with a name and password. Join that Wi-Fi on the other device and open the URL on the dashboard, no router needed.

**What data does ScreenExtend collect?**
None is stored. Settings stay on your device; a session only exchanges what's needed to set up the connection, then it's gone.
